mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen for two consecutive weeks (t-2w to t-0w, from -53.1 to -40.6), indicating a self-reinforcing recovery in shopping and recreation footfall driven by eased caution and pent-up demand, which should continue over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -53.1 to -40.6 over the last two weeks
failure_condition: If mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the last 28 days despite two prior weeks of improvement, the momentum mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rebound in WORKPLACES mobility signals loosening of pandemic-era workplace restrictions; once WORKPLACES rises by more than 5 points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks, commuter-linked retail footfall near offices rises within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises more than 5 points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -43.6 to -36.4 over the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within two weeks of WORKPLACES crossing the +5 point weekly recovery threshold in two consecutive instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous recovery in TRANSIT and PARKS alongside a declining RESIDENTIAL trend indicates a broad behavioral shift away from home-confinement toward combined outdoor and transit-based activity, which jointly amplifies retail and recreation visits beyond what any single series predicts alone.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and PARKS both rise while RESIDENTIAL falls in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose sharply from -43.9 to -24.1 while RESIDENTIAL fell from 14.3 to 9.9
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 4 weeks even though TRANSIT and PARKS both rose and RESIDENTIAL fell concurrently for two or more weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp PARKS rebound (from -43.9 to -24.1) reflects early seasonal warming in late winter Lombardy, which draws people outdoors and subsequently increases nearby retail and recreation visits as outdoor activity habituates people to leaving home.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS increased by nearly 15 points in the most recent week
failure_condition: If PARKS continues rising but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days fails to exceed the last 28 days, the seasonal spillover mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility stabilizing near its least negative level (-18.9 at t-0w after a trough of -28.6) signals reduced health-risk aversion among residents, which should translate into higher discretionary retail visits within one week as essential-trip caution relaxes first.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM improves by more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from -23.3 to -18.9 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within one week following a GROCERY_PHARM improvement exceeding 5 points.

mechanism_narrative: The steady decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility (from 14.3 to 9.9 over three weeks) indicates households are spending less time at home, which mechanically frees time for retail and recreation trips over the subsequent two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls for three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined each week from 13.3 to 9.9
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the following two weeks despite three consecutive weeks of RESIDENTIAL decline.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility were to fall below its prior trough of -47.1 again, this would indicate renewed restriction tightening or a resurgence of infection fears, which would suppress retail and recreation mobility over the following two weeks even if recent trends have been improving.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -47.1 (its prior four-week low) in any coming week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT reached a trough of -47.1 at t-2w before recovering to -37.1
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise even after TRANSIT falls below the -47.1 threshold, rejecting the restriction-tightening mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent weekly improvement in WORKPLACES mobility reflects a gradual seasonal return to office routines after the winter holiday and Omicron-wave disruption, which should modestly lift weekday retail visits within one week as commuting patterns normalize.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -43.6 to -36.4 over the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within one week of continued WORKPLACES improvement, indicating no short-horizon linkage between office return and retail activity.
